subject: PrivInfra: module artifact signing, CI contracts, and preflight matrix
messages:
From: natalie@edgeops.io
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2025-08-30T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivInfra: module artifact signing, CI contracts, and preflight matrix

Hi team,

Thanks for taking this on. PrismHealth is getting ready to onboard a private deployment and our security team is asking for explicit artifact provenance for any Terraform/Helm/Ansible artifacts we deliver into their air-gapped environment. They want:

- Signed Terraform modules (artifact-level signature + git tag attestation)
- Helm charts with provenance files and signatures
- A CI acceptance matrix that the on-prem GitLab runner can validate pre-deploy (network-limited)

I've attached a quick checklist we used on a prior engagement — it's a starting point (iac-provenance-checklist.xlsx). Can you confirm what signing approach Redwood prefers (cosign/sigstore, internal KMS signing, or both) and how that fits with your private deploy flow?

Two immediate asks from PrismHealth:
1) A proposed list of CI jobs that will run in their staging runner (they want to vet before we hand over).
2) A minimal preflight matrix they can include in their runbook to gate production.

Can you loop in whoever will own the Ansible role publishing? We should align on how credentials and secrets needed for signing are handled given their air-gapped constraints.

Best,
Natalie
Head of Integrations, EdgeOps (contractor)
[Attachment: iac-provenance-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
To: natalie@edgeops.io
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-08-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivInfra: module artifact signing, CI contracts, and preflight matrix

Natalie — thanks, this is helpful. High-level answers and proposals below.

1) Artifact signing approach
- Primary: sigstore/cosign for container/helm chart signing and OIDC-attested artifact signatures.
- Terraform modules: we will emit signed tarballs and a SLSA-style attestation linked to the git tag. For extra assurance we can cross-sign using our central HSM (KMS-backed key) and provide the public verifier key to PrismHealth.
- Ansible roles: publish as signed tarballs into their airgap bundle; include checksum and signature file.

2) CI contract and acceptance jobs (proposed)
- job: lint-templates (terraform fmt/validate, helm lint)
- job: unit->plan (terraform plan with minimal vars, fail on drift)
- job: build-artifact (helm package / role tarball) + cosign sign -> push to artifact-bucket
- job: attest (generate SLSA attestation, sign with build key, attach to release)
- job: preflight-check (runs the preflight matrix; exits non-zero if any compulsory checks fail)

I've sketched a GitLab CI fragment and a recommended job set in the attached proposed-ci-jobs.yaml. For private deployments we expect PrismHealth to run only the verification and preflight jobs inside their air-gapped runner. The build/sign steps can be done in our hosted CI and the signed artifacts + attestations transferred to a staging bucket (or a signed release bundle) for them to consume.

3) Secrets & KMS handling
- Pattern: sign in our hosted CI with ephemeral OIDC-issued creds to access sigstore; for cross-signing we use a KMS-backed HSM key that is strictly controlled and audited.
- For on-prem verification they only need the public keys (we'll provide keyset + verification steps). No private keys leave Redwood.

4) Interface freeze & timelines
- If PrismHealth wants a freeze on module interfaces, we can aim for 2025-09-15 for a code freeze for the modules in scope (assuming approvals this week).

Next steps:
- Irene, can you confirm network feasibility for verification jobs in their runner?
- Mina, can you validate the proposed signing workflow against our policy & add any compliance checks?
- Natalie, we'll upload the CI fragment and a formal preflight matrix CSV for them to review.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | ev_hart@redwood.com
[Attachment: proposed-ci-jobs.yaml (text)]

On Fri, Aug 30, 2025 at 11:03 AM evelyn.hart@redwood.com wrote:
> For private deployments we expect PrismHealth to run only the verification and preflight jobs inside their air-gapped runner.

Quick network/ops notes from my side:
- PrismHealth's staging runner is behind a dedicated VLAN and only allows egress to an approved artifact-staging S3 endpoint via a proxy. We'll need to ensure verification scripts can work with that proxy (curl/sha256sum/cosign verify should be fine, but we need to avoid any OIDC flows that require outbound calls to public identity providers).
- Recommendation: deliver a verification bundle that contains: verifier binary (cosign), static CA bundle, signed artifacts, attestations, and a lightweight verification script that runs offline. This avoids requiring the runner to call back to sigstore services.
- For Ansible, the roles will reference secrets from Vault. PrismHealth uses an on-prem HashiVault and wants exact instructions for configuring read-only verification tokens. We should provide a rotate-and-revoke recipe in the runbook.

I've prepared a first draft of the acceptance matrix and added it as ci-acceptance-matrix.csv (columns: check_id, artifact_type, mandatory/optional, runtime, notes). I'm attaching and linking to JIRA-PRIV-4823 for the work items.

Operational blockers:
- If PrismHealth requires us to produce signed attestations that validate with their internal CA only, we need a short meeting with their infra team to exchange trust roots.
- Timing: I can finalize the offline verification bundle if we lock the list of artifacts by 2025-09-08.

Irene Choi
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ci-acceptance-matrix.csv (csv)]

Evelyn / team — this looks good, thanks for the detailed plan. A few quick confirmation items from PrismHealth: 

- They prefer an offline verification bundle as Irene suggested.
- They will accept cosign-verified artifacts plus our HSM cross-signature public key.
- Freeze date of 2025-09-15 is acceptable if we can produce the verification bundle by 2025-09-08 (Irene's timeline).

Alan (cc'd) — can you confirm the internal security team will be available next week for a short trust-root exchange?

If everyone agrees, we'll schedule a 30-minute sync next Tuesday to hand off the first draft bundle and the updated acceptance matrix. I'll also raise a PrismHealth procurement work item for the signed artifact transfer process.

Thanks,
